This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. SpaceX has been pouring money into
artificial intelligence, and now the company reports that AI is its biggest source of revenue.
NPR's John Ruich has more.
In a quarterly earnings report, the company said its revenues were up 161 percent from
the same quarter last year, beating expectations. Revenue from AI leapt ninefold to $7.6 billion,
or a little more than half of the total. The company has its own AI model, called Grok,
and it rents out data center space. Starlink, its satellite internet business, grew its
customer base during the period, and the company says it's making progress with the recoverability
of its heavy-lift rocket, called Starship. Meanwhile, CEO Elon Musk says special committees
at SpaceX and his EV company Tesla are discussing a possible merger.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Marseille is the latest French city to impose a curfew after devastating riots and violence
over the weekend, and NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
Parts of Paris, as well as Lille, Nice and Lyon, are under curfew for a second night.
The French government has admitted it was unprepared for the large number of protesters
Saturday and the roving bands of youths who took advantage of the situation to burn and
pillage. The student protest that began a month ago demanding better facilities and
more teachers has ballooned into a wider movement over the cost of living and social injustice.
An editorial in Le Monde newspaper said October 17 will likely go down as a symbol of the collapse
of the Macron presidency. Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
A New Jersey food importer filed a lawsuit today challenging President Trump's use of
a depression-era law to levy a 50 percent tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.
The power has never been used in a trade dispute, let alone tested in court. The Gellert Global
Group, which imports Canadian cheese, filed the suit with the U.S. Court of International
Trade. Beef could play a decisive role in this year's midterm elections. Ground beef
cost $6.80 a pound, nearly a dollar more adjusted for inflation than it did when President Trump
took office. But beef producers are also feeling the pain, and it could sway tight races in
even red states, as NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben reports.
President Trump in August expanded the quota for lean beef trimmings that could come into
the country under lower tariffs. It was a move intended to lower ground beef prices,
but it made life tougher for beef producers. Scott Birker raises cattle in eastern Iowa.
That surprise with a very volatile market already with a tight supply hurts us really,
really fast and really, really hard.
Trump's beef import policy has become an important topic in Iowa's closed Senate race, and political
strategists say it could also affect the state's House and gubernatorial races. Several more
major beef-producing states are also midterm battlegrounds, including Nebraska, Texas,
and Kansas. Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
The U.S. stock market rose today. The Dow rose more than 1 percent. This is NPR News.
Voters in Alberta overwhelmingly backed remaining in Canada. The result boosts Prime Minister
Mark Carney's push for national unity amid trade tensions with the U.S. The referendum
wasn't a direct vote on independence, but would have set Alberta on a path toward a
future separation vote. Separatist leaders say their movement won't disappear. Nigeria
has confirmed the country's first Ebola case in the capital city. As NPR's Jonathan Lambert
reports, health officials are saying the current outbreak is now the most geographically widespread
ever.
Nigerian health officials confirmed on Tuesday that a woman who'd been receiving care at
a hospital in Abuja tested positive for Ebola. She'd recently arrived in the city of over
2 million on an international flight from Uganda, officials say. Uganda reported 20 Ebola cases
early in this year's outbreak, but was declared Ebola-free in late August. It's unclear where
the patient got infected. Health officials in Nigeria have already identified 44 close
contacts of the woman and are monitoring those who may have been exposed. Nigeria's first
case comes days after the virus arrived in Kenya, where nine people have tested positive.
The Democratic Republic of Congo remains the outbreak's epicenter, reporting over 9,000
cases and 4,600 deaths since May. Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Police in California are investigating the theft of trading cards worth at least $963,000
from a FedEx truck. The truck was broken into on October 13th outside a company called Professional
Sports Authenticator that verifies memorabilia. The Santa Ana Police Department says Pokemon
and sports cards were among the stolen items. This is NPR.
